clue.text: Inclined in all directions, as notes by a student

parts.note: qua is Latin-derived for 'in the capacity of', i.e. as
L is a learner, the plate a student driver wears

explanation.surface: A geology-sounding description of tilted strata compared with a student's scattered notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' looks like lecture jottings, but they are musical quavers.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaquaversal is a geological term for strata dipping outward from a centre in every direction.

clue.text: Sex training is not entirely off the menu

indicators.note: the answer is only part of the words sex training, so it lies within them

explanation.surface: A risqué remark that sex instruction is not quite banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off the menu' suggests forbidden, but it means ordered separately rather than from the set menu.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is an item charged separately, outside the set menu.

clue.text: Sylvan isthmus in (usually this) region

parts.note: a neck of land is a narrow isthmus

explanation.surface: A geography note about a wooded isthmus in one's own area.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed 'usually this' reminds the solver that the phrase usually comes as 'this neck of the woods'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a person's local area or district.

clue.text: City of sausages, sauce and stuff

definitions.meaning: a large smoked sausage takes its name from this city
bolognese meat sauce is named after the city
stuff as in stuff and nonsense, spelt baloney or boloney

explanation.surface: A guide to an Italian city's food: its sausages, its sauce and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' looks like 'and so on' but is a fourth definition: stuff and nonsense, the sound of baloney.
explanation.definitionFit: The city's name is also the sausage, the sauce's root and a near-homophone of baloney, nonsense.

clue.text: Seaside region right for setter to struggle with …

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I
to vie is to struggle or compete
the dots run on into the next clue, whose opening word is god: the Egyptian sun god Ra

explanation.surface: The setter wrestling with a seaside resort, to be continued.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the clue to the next, borrowing 'god' from it to give RA, the Egyptian sun god.
explanation.definitionFit: A riviera is a coastal strip of resorts, a seaside region.

clue.text: … god of periods with little change

indicators.note: a small change shuffles just two letters of the word for periods

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a deity presiding over times that barely change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with little change' is the anagram signal: swapping two letters of HOURS makes the god.
explanation.definitionFit: Horus is the falcon-headed sky god of ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Land Geraint Evans without first three of seven shows

indicators.note: the names are put on show rearranged, displaying a new arrangement
takes the opening three letters of the word seven

explanation.surface: Welsh opera singer Sir Geraint Evans performing in seven shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' tells you to remove SEV, the first three letters of 'seven', from the letters of GERAINT EVANS; 'shows' rearranges what remains. Geraint Evans was a famous Welsh bass-baritone.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a South American country, a land.

clue.text: The Greek room

definitions.meaning: ... Greek is the classical dialect of Athens
a room directly under the roof

explanation.surface: A loft space with a classical Greek owner.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic means Athenian, the classical Greek, and is also a room in the roof space.

clue.text: Power to get things done on line for good long time

parts.note: an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A description of getting things done through a lasting line of influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the line to what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverage is influence or power used to achieve an end.

clue.text: Principal Guy (with Dolls) — Scotsman holding flowers under heaven

indicators.note: in a down clue the second part sits below the first
the Scotsman word clasps the flowers within it

parts.note: mon is a Scots form of man

explanation.surface: Introducing the lead man of a musical, with flowers and a Scot below the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' and 'Dolls' point to the musical Guys and Dolls, whose leading man is the gambler Sky Masterson.
explanation.definitionFit: Sky Masterson is the principal male character, a guy, in Guys and Dolls.

clue.text: Posh friend, willing to take part and start to go homeward

parts.note: if you are on for something you are willing to join in

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An upper-class chum keen to join in and head for home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' simply links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Up-along is a West Country dialect word for homeward or up the road.

clue.text: Upsetting the old, first to stick neck out, I favoured Nature rather than Nurture

definitions.text: I favoured Nature rather than Nurture

indicators.note: turning over the word for the old reverses its letters

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the

indicators.note: takes the first letter of stick
neck goes out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A psychologist boasting of sticking his neck out against tradition on the nature versus nurture debate.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in the first person: the answer himself speaking. Hans Eysenck was a psychologist who stressed heredity over environment.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Eysenck argued that intelligence and personality were largely inherited, siding with nature.

clue.text: Call number on question of identification

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A phone call with a numbered identity check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To call on someone is to visit them.

clue.text: Whistle-blower mends life's fuse

indicators.note: mending reworks the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: An informant who repairs the fuse of a life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistle-blower' suggests an informant, but here it means a woman who whistles, a stage whistler.
explanation.definitionFit: A siffleuse is a female whistler, literally one who blows a whistle tune.

clue.text: Chaos theory? It brings nothing less than chaos in random access memory

indicators.note: random signals the letters are jumbled
one word taken away from another

parts.note: random access memory is RAM, the clue reusing the familiar phrase

explanation.surface: A computing joke: anarchy rampant in a computer's RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchism is the political theory favouring no government, jokingly a theory of chaos.

clue.text: Spanish gentleman takes taxi to go round in France

parts.note: aller is French for to go, signalled by 'in France'

explanation.surface: A Spanish nobleman hailing a cab for a trip round France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in France' tells you 'to go' is translated into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Caballero is Spanish for a gentleman or knight.

clue.text: Display of the foregoing without meat makes one crack

indicators.note: outside: the riot word goes round the meat word

parts.note: the previous clue's answer, chaos, on display is a riot

explanation.surface: A vegetarian chaos display that ends with a sharp crack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle shot makes a crack, a single sharp report.

clue.text: Wall builder got North wind to back

indicators.note: back means go backwards, so north and wind are read in reverse

explanation.surface: Building a wall against the north wind.
explanation.walkthrough: Hadrian's Wall crosses northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Emperor Hadrian built the wall across northern Britain.

clue.text: Name for girl model, somewhat hard one

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A girl model described as rather tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabitha is a girl's given name.

clue.text: See 27
Let vocal be vocal

indicators.note: to be vocal is to speak, so the word is said aloud

explanation.surface: A singing direction letting a voice be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'vocal's look alike but one gives the word and the other says it is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Let as a past participle means permitted.

clue.text: See 3
Uncooperative sloven backed to go fast

indicators.note: something backed has moved backwards, so the sloven word is read from its end to its start

explanation.surface: A lazy person suddenly forced to hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshie is British slang for rebellious, from Bolshevik.

clue.text: Search takes in a place regularly 13ed

indicators.note: the search word contains the letter

explanation.surface: A search covering somewhere often visited.
explanation.walkthrough: '13ed' means visited, the answer to 13 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunt is a place one frequently visits.

clue.text: Mo is hurt playing joker

indicators.note: playing about with the letters rearranges them

explanation.surface: Mo is hurt while playing a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorist is a writer or performer of comic material, a joker.

clue.text: Transatlantic power blocs invest queen with horse

indicators.note: invest means clothe, surround

parts.note: the European Union is EU, one power bloc
Q is queen in chess or cards
the United States is US, on the other side of the Atlantic

explanation.surface: Europe and America investing the queen with a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Equus is Latin for horse and also a Peter Shaffer play.
explanation.definitionFit: Equus is the Latin word and genus name for horse.

clue.text: Ban ambitious sons: get prepared for life on the river

indicators.note: the words are prepared, arranged into a new form

explanation.surface: Banning ambitious young men, telling them to get ready.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is from The Wind in the Willows: 'simply messing about in boats'.
explanation.definitionFit: Messing about in boats is idle leisure on the river.
